edges.description: Disrupted glypican-mediated developmental signaling perturbs craniofacial and lacrimal patterning.
Disrupted developmental signaling perturbs distal limb and digit formation.
Craniofacial developmental abnormalities produce the recognizable facial phenotype.
Altered craniofacial patterning leads to frontal bossing and a prominent forehead.
Altered midfacial patterning causes a flat midface and midface hypoplasia.
Disrupted frontonasal morphogenesis produces a broad nose.
Abnormal nasal bridge development produces a depressed and broad nasal bridge.
Altered frontonasal patterning causes widely spaced eyes.
Craniofacial dysmorphism includes downturned oral commissures.
Impaired lacrimal morphogenesis can result in complete agenesis of the lacrimal puncta.
Abnormal distal limb development contributes to shortened digits.
Distal limb patterning defects produce a broad first toe.
Distal phalangeal morphogenesis defects produce broad terminal phalanges.

nodes.description: Keipert syndrome is caused by pathogenic GPC4 variants that destabilize or truncate glypican 4, a cell-surface heparan sulfate proteoglycan that regulates growth-factor signaling during development. Pathogenic alleles include final-exon C-terminal truncating variants (which cause loss of N-linked glycosylation at Asn514 and the glycosylphosphatidylinositol [GPI] anchor site at Ser529 and reduce protein stability) as well as earlier nonsense and canonical splice-site variants, perturbing morphogenetic signaling gradients required for normal craniofacial, lacrimal, and limb patterning.
